lesson_1.title: Lesson 1: Wartime Pledges: McMahon, Sykes-Picot & Balfour (Stages 1–3) (50 mins)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Run the baseline Do Now on Eastern Mediterranean and Red Sea geography, First World War dates (1914–18), empires and colonies, and Jerusalem’s sacred significance to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
phases.instruction: Run the baseline Do Now on Eastern Mediterranean and Red Sea geography, First World War dates (1914–18), empires and colonies, and Jerusalem’s sacred significance to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

phases.label: Teacher Exposition
phases.activity: Map Ottoman rule across the Middle East and explain why wartime desperation led Britain into three clashing commitments: McMahon’s October 1915 letters to Sharif Hussein, the secret May 1916 Sykes-Picot partition with France, and Arthur Balfour’s November 1917 pledge of a Jewish national home.
phases.instruction: Map Ottoman rule across the Middle East and explain why wartime desperation led Britain into three clashing commitments: McMahon’s October 1915 letters to Sharif Hussein, the secret May 1916 Sykes-Picot partition with France, and Arthur Balfour’s November 1917 pledge of a Jewish national home.

phases.phase: Phase 3: Shared Reading & Verso Spine Stages 1–3 (17 mins)
phases.label: Shared Reading & Spine
phases.activity: Read Narrative Stages 1–3 aloud as a class, tracking why Arab leaders felt betrayed by Sykes-Picot and how the Balfour Declaration created contradictory promises, then complete full-sentence responses in Workbook Verso Spine stages 1–3.
phases.instruction: Read Narrative Stages 1–3 aloud as a class, tracking why Arab leaders felt betrayed by Sykes-Picot and how the Balfour Declaration created contradictory promises, then complete full-sentence responses in Workbook Verso Spine stages 1–3.

phases.phase: Phase 4: Hinge Diagnostic & Source Scrutiny (10 mins)
phases.label: Hinge Check
phases.activity: Compare Source A (McMahon’s exclusion of land “west of the districts of Damascus”) with Source B (the straight imperial borders of the Sykes-Picot map) to test why Palestine became contested before 1918.
phases.instruction: Compare Source A (McMahon’s exclusion of land “west of the districts of Damascus”) with Source B (the straight imperial borders of the Sykes-Picot map) to test why Palestine became contested before 1918.

lesson_2.title: Lesson 2: The British Mandate, Arab Revolt & 1939 White Paper (Stages 4–5 & Writing) (50 mins)
lesson_2.focus: The British Mandate, Arab Revolt & 1939 White Paper (Stages 4–5 & Writing)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Retrieve the three wartime pledges from Lesson 1 (McMahon-Hussein 1915, Sykes-Picot 1916, Balfour Declaration 1917) and check why both Arab nationalists and Zionists claimed British backing.
phases.instruction: Retrieve the three wartime pledges from Lesson 1 (McMahon-Hussein 1915, Sykes-Picot 1916, Balfour Declaration 1917) and check why both Arab nationalists and Zionists claimed British backing.

phases.label: Narrative & Sources
phases.activity: Read Stages 4–5 on the 1922 League of Nations Mandate, 1930s Jewish immigration fleeing Nazi persecution, the 1936–39 Arab Revolt, and the May 1939 White Paper (75,000 five-year cap), then examine Sources C, D, and E on why both communities rejected the White Paper.
phases.instruction: Read Stages 4–5 on the 1922 League of Nations Mandate, 1930s Jewish immigration fleeing Nazi persecution, the 1936–39 Arab Revolt, and the May 1939 White Paper (75,000 five-year cap), then examine Sources C, D, and E on why both communities rejected the White Paper.

phases.label: Exam Writing
phases.activity: Introduce Paper 2 Period Study consequence paragraphs (two 4-mark consequences = 8 marks) by drafting a consequence paragraph on the 1939 White Paper alongside the Evaluative Ranking Ladder weighing wartime pledges, 1930s immigration, and 1939 policy.
phases.instruction: Introduce Paper 2 Period Study consequence paragraphs (two 4-mark consequences = 8 marks) by drafting a consequence paragraph on the 1939 White Paper alongside the Evaluative Ranking Ladder weighing wartime pledges, 1930s immigration, and 1939 policy.

phases.label: Consolidate & DIRT
phases.activity: Peer-check each paragraph for a clear consequence statement supported by precise 1936–39 Mandate evidence, then verify justification sentences on the Ranking Ladder.
phases.instruction: Peer-check each paragraph for a clear consequence statement supported by precise 1936–39 Mandate evidence, then verify justification sentences on the Ranking Ladder.

lesson_1.title: Lesson 1: Post-War Quotas, Insurgency & King David Hotel (Stages 1–3) (50 mins)
lesson_1.focus: Post-War Quotas, Insurgency & King David Hotel (Stages 1–3)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Complete the spaced Do Now retrieving pre-1945 Mandate pledges, the May 1939 White Paper quota, Allied victory in 1945, Holocaust displacement in Europe, and Britain’s post-war economic exhaustion under Clement Attlee.
phases.instruction: Complete the spaced Do Now retrieving pre-1945 Mandate pledges, the May 1939 White Paper quota, Allied victory in 1945, Holocaust displacement in Europe, and Britain’s post-war economic exhaustion under Clement Attlee.

phases.label: Teacher Exposition
phases.activity: Explain why Ernest Bevin enforced the 1,500 monthly immigration cap to preserve Arab oil and strategic ties while Harry Truman demanded 100,000 entry certificates, driving the Haganah, Irgun, and Lehi into the October 1945 United Resistance Movement.
phases.instruction: Explain why Ernest Bevin enforced the 1,500 monthly immigration cap to preserve Arab oil and strategic ties while Harry Truman demanded 100,000 entry certificates, driving the Haganah, Irgun, and Lehi into the October 1945 United Resistance Movement.

phases.phase: Phase 3: Shared Reading & Verso Spine Stages 1–3 (17 mins)
phases.label: Shared Reading & Spine
phases.activity: Shared reading of Stages 1–3 covering European DP camps, paramilitary railway and radar sabotage, Operation Agatha, and the Irgun’s 22 July 1946 bombing of British headquarters at the King David Hotel (91 killed), completing Verso Spine stages 1–3.
phases.instruction: Shared reading of Stages 1–3 covering European DP camps, paramilitary railway and radar sabotage, Operation Agatha, and the Irgun’s 22 July 1946 bombing of British headquarters at the King David Hotel (91 killed), completing Verso Spine stages 1–3.

phases.phase: Phase 4: Hinge Diagnostic & Source Scrutiny (10 mins)
phases.label: Hinge Check
phases.activity: Scrutinise Source A (Bergen-Belsen survivors, 1945) and Source B (Jewish leaders detained at Latrun after Operation Agatha, June 1946) to diagnose why compromise between British policing and Zionist immigration demands broke down.
phases.instruction: Scrutinise Source A (Bergen-Belsen survivors, 1945) and Source B (Jewish leaders detained at Latrun after Operation Agatha, June 1946) to diagnose why compromise between British policing and Zionist immigration demands broke down.

lesson_2.title: Lesson 2: Sergeants Affair, SS Exodus & UN Resolution 181 (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Writing) (50 mins)
lesson_2.focus: Sergeants Affair, SS Exodus & UN Resolution 181 (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Writing)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Spaced recall check on Bevin’s 1,500 monthly limit, the United Resistance Movement, and the July 1946 King David Hotel bombing before introducing the crises of summer 1947.
phases.instruction: Spaced recall check on Bevin’s 1,500 monthly limit, the United Resistance Movement, and the July 1946 King David Hotel bombing before introducing the crises of summer 1947.

phases.label: Narrative & Sources
phases.activity: Read Stages 4–5 on Britain’s £100 million garrison burden, the July 1947 Sergeants Affair in Netanya, the Royal Navy interception of SS Exodus 1947, and UN Resolution 181 (November 1947 partition: ~55–56% Jewish state, ~43% Arab state, international Jerusalem), interrogating Sources C, D, and E.
phases.instruction: Read Stages 4–5 on Britain’s £100 million garrison burden, the July 1947 Sergeants Affair in Netanya, the Royal Navy interception of SS Exodus 1947, and UN Resolution 181 (November 1947 partition: ~55–56% Jewish state, ~43% Arab state, international Jerusalem), interrogating Sources C, D, and E.

phases.label: Exam Writing
phases.activity: Timed Edexcel Paper 2 practice: complete two 4-mark consequence responses (Q1: King David Hotel bombing, 1946; UN Resolution 181, 1947 [8m pair]) and the 8-mark Importance response (Q3: importance of conflicting Jewish and Arab demands for Britain’s 1947 withdrawal).
phases.instruction: Timed Edexcel Paper 2 practice: complete two 4-mark consequence responses (Q1: King David Hotel bombing, 1946; UN Resolution 181, 1947 [8m pair]) and the 8-mark Importance response (Q3: importance of conflicting Jewish and Arab demands for Britain’s 1947 withdrawal).

phases.label: Consolidate & DIRT
phases.activity: Model how a high-tariff Paper 2 Importance paragraph links X directly to Y (how irreconcilable demands made Mandate rule ungovernable and forced handover to UNSCOP), with green-pen DIRT.
phases.instruction: Model how a high-tariff Paper 2 Importance paragraph links X directly to Y (how irreconcilable demands made Mandate rule ungovernable and forced handover to UNSCOP), with green-pen DIRT.

lesson_1.title: Lesson 1: 14 May 1948, First UN Truce & The Nakba (Stages 1–3) (50 mins)
lesson_1.focus: 14 May 1948, First UN Truce & The Nakba (Stages 1–3)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Complete the Do Now retrieving Bevin’s immigration limits, Menachem Begin’s Irgun insurgency, the SS Exodus 1947 scandal, and UN Resolution 181’s partition terms from KT 1.1.
phases.instruction: Complete the Do Now retrieving Bevin’s immigration limits, Menachem Begin’s Irgun insurgency, the SS Exodus 1947 scandal, and UN Resolution 181’s partition terms from KT 1.1.

phases.label: Teacher Exposition
phases.activity: Trace the sequence from British withdrawal and David Ben-Gurion’s 14 May 1948 proclamation of Israel to the 15 May entry of Egyptian, Jordanian, Syrian, Iraqi, and Lebanese armies, highlighting how the June 1948 First UN Truce and Czech arms reversed the military balance.
phases.instruction: Trace the sequence from British withdrawal and David Ben-Gurion’s 14 May 1948 proclamation of Israel to the 15 May entry of Egyptian, Jordanian, Syrian, Iraqi, and Lebanese armies, highlighting how the June 1948 First UN Truce and Czech arms reversed the military balance.

phases.phase: Phase 3: Shared Reading & Verso Spine Stages 1–3 (17 mins)
phases.label: Shared Reading & Spine
phases.activity: Read Stages 1–3 on Israel’s declaration, unified IDF command and Czech weapons during the four-week truce, and the Palestinian refugee crisis (Al-Nakba, Deir Yassin, over 700,000 displaced, and UNRWA’s creation), completing Verso Spine stages 1–3.
phases.instruction: Read Stages 1–3 on Israel’s declaration, unified IDF command and Czech weapons during the four-week truce, and the Palestinian refugee crisis (Al-Nakba, Deir Yassin, over 700,000 displaced, and UNRWA’s creation), completing Verso Spine stages 1–3.

phases.phase: Phase 4: Hinge Diagnostic & Source Scrutiny (10 mins)
phases.label: Hinge Check
phases.activity: Compare Source A (rival Arab and Israeli explanations of the 15 May 1948 invasion) with Source B (the Czech-supplied Avia S-199 fighter, June 1948) to test why Arab disunity and Israeli rearmament turned the war.
phases.instruction: Compare Source A (rival Arab and Israeli explanations of the 15 May 1948 invasion) with Source B (the Czech-supplied Avia S-199 fighter, June 1948) to test why Arab disunity and Israeli rearmament turned the war.

lesson_2.title: Lesson 2: 1949 Rhodes Armistices & Law of Return (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Narrative Writing) (50 mins)
lesson_2.focus: 1949 Rhodes Armistices & Law of Return (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Narrative Writing)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Quick retrieval check on 14 May 1948, the June 1948 First Truce, Czech arms, and Al-Nakba alongside synoptic links to UN Resolution 181.
phases.instruction: Quick retrieval check on 14 May 1948, the June 1948 First Truce, Czech arms, and Al-Nakba alongside synoptic links to UN Resolution 181.

phases.label: Narrative & Sources
phases.activity: Read Stages 4–5 on Dr Ralph Bunche’s 1949 Rhodes Armistice Agreements (the Green Line leaving Israel with 78%, Jordan holding the West Bank and East Jerusalem, and Egypt administering Gaza) and the July 1950 Law of Return, analysing Sources C (Khan Yunis camp), D (Arab Legion in Jerusalem), and E (Haifa arrivals).
phases.instruction: Read Stages 4–5 on Dr Ralph Bunche’s 1949 Rhodes Armistice Agreements (the Green Line leaving Israel with 78%, Jordan holding the West Bank and East Jerusalem, and Egypt administering Gaza) and the July 1950 Law of Return, analysing Sources C (Khan Yunis camp), D (Arab Legion in Jerusalem), and E (Haifa arrivals).

phases.label: Exam Writing
phases.activity: Timed Edexcel Paper 2 practice: complete the two 4-mark consequence questions (Palestinian refugee status; 1950 Law of Return) and the 8-mark Analytical Narrative (Q2: analysing key events of the 1948–49 Arab-Israeli War).
phases.instruction: Timed Edexcel Paper 2 practice: complete the two 4-mark consequence questions (Palestinian refugee status; 1950 Law of Return) and the 8-mark Analytical Narrative (Q2: analysing key events of the 1948–49 Arab-Israeli War).

phases.label: Consolidate & DIRT
phases.activity: Audit pupils’ 8-mark narratives for three chronologically ordered stages (May 1948 outbreak -> June truce & Czech rearmament -> 1949 Rhodes Green Line) joined by explicit causal linking phrases.
phases.instruction: Audit pupils’ 8-mark narratives for three chronologically ordered stages (May 1948 outbreak -> June truce & Czech rearmament -> 1949 Rhodes Green Line) joined by explicit causal linking phrases.

lesson_1.title: Lesson 1: Gaza Raid, Czech Arms & Suez Nationalisation (Stages 1–3) (50 mins)
lesson_1.focus: Gaza Raid, Czech Arms & Suez Nationalisation (Stages 1–3)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Complete the spaced Do Now retrieving 14 May 1948, Count Bernadotte and the First Truce, Al-Nakba, and the 1949 Rhodes Armistice borders from KT 1.2.
phases.instruction: Complete the spaced Do Now retrieving 14 May 1948, Count Bernadotte and the First Truce, Al-Nakba, and the 1949 Rhodes Armistice borders from KT 1.2.

phases.label: Teacher Exposition
phases.activity: Contextualise Colonel Gamal Abdel Nasser’s Pan-Arab nationalism within the Cold War, tracing the causal chain from Israel’s February 1955 Gaza Raid to the September 1955 Czech Arms Deal, cancelled US/British Aswan High Dam loans, and the 26 July 1956 nationalisation of the Suez Canal.
phases.instruction: Contextualise Colonel Gamal Abdel Nasser’s Pan-Arab nationalism within the Cold War, tracing the causal chain from Israel’s February 1955 Gaza Raid to the September 1955 Czech Arms Deal, cancelled US/British Aswan High Dam loans, and the 26 July 1956 nationalisation of the Suez Canal.

phases.phase: Phase 3: Shared Reading & Verso Spine Stages 1–3 (17 mins)
phases.label: Shared Reading & Spine
phases.activity: Read Stages 1–3 and complete Workbook Verso Spine stages 1–3, checking that pupils connect Nasser’s blockade of the Straits of Tiran and Aswan funding crisis directly to canal nationalisation.
phases.instruction: Read Stages 1–3 and complete Workbook Verso Spine stages 1–3, checking that pupils connect Nasser’s blockade of the Straits of Tiran and Aswan funding crisis directly to canal nationalisation.

phases.phase: Phase 4: Hinge Diagnostic & Source Scrutiny (10 mins)
phases.label: Hinge Check
phases.activity: Interrogate Source A (rival readings of the February 1955 Gaza Raid) and Source B (Nasser with Nehru at Bandung and the September 1955 Czech Arms Deal) to check why Cold War conditions escalated a border clash.
phases.instruction: Interrogate Source A (rival readings of the February 1955 Gaza Raid) and Source B (Nasser with Nehru at Bandung and the September 1955 Czech Arms Deal) to check why Cold War conditions escalated a border clash.

lesson_2.title: Lesson 2: Secret Sèvres Plot, US Pressure & UNEF (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Narrative Writing) (50 mins)
lesson_2.focus: Secret Sèvres Plot, US Pressure & UNEF (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Narrative Writing)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Retrieve the Gaza Raid, 1955 Czech Arms Deal, Aswan Dam loan withdrawal, and 26 July 1956 Suez nationalisation from Lesson 1.
phases.instruction: Retrieve the Gaza Raid, 1955 Czech Arms Deal, Aswan Dam loan withdrawal, and 26 July 1956 Suez nationalisation from Lesson 1.

phases.label: Narrative & Sources
phases.activity: Read Stages 4–5 on the October 1956 Secret Protocol of Sèvres (Anthony Eden, Guy Mollet, David Ben-Gurion), Operation Musketeer, President Eisenhower’s financial and UN pressure forcing Anglo-French retreat, UNEF’s Sinai deployment, and the 1958 UAR, examining Sources C, D, and E.
phases.instruction: Read Stages 4–5 on the October 1956 Secret Protocol of Sèvres (Anthony Eden, Guy Mollet, David Ben-Gurion), Operation Musketeer, President Eisenhower’s financial and UN pressure forcing Anglo-French retreat, UNEF’s Sinai deployment, and the 1958 UAR, examining Sources C, D, and E.

phases.label: Exam Writing
phases.activity: Timed Edexcel Paper 2 practice: answer the two 4-mark consequence questions (February 1955 Gaza Raid; 1956 Suez Crisis for Britain and France) and the 8-mark Analytical Narrative (Q2: analysing the key events of the 1956 Suez Crisis).
phases.instruction: Timed Edexcel Paper 2 practice: answer the two 4-mark consequence questions (February 1955 Gaza Raid; 1956 Suez Crisis for Britain and France) and the 8-mark Analytical Narrative (Q2: analysing the key events of the 1956 Suez Crisis).

phases.label: Consolidate & DIRT
phases.activity: Self-assess against Paper 2 narrative criteria: verify causal links from Aswan/nationalisation -> Sèvres collusion & Sinai/Port Said landings -> Eisenhower’s ultimatum & UNEF withdrawal.
phases.instruction: Self-assess against Paper 2 narrative criteria: verify causal links from Aswan/nationalisation -> Sèvres collusion & Sinai/Port Said landings -> Eisenhower’s ultimatum & UNEF withdrawal.

lesson_1.title: Lesson 1: 1964 Cairo Summit, River Jordan Water & Fatah Raids (Stages 1–3) (50 mins)
lesson_1.focus: 1964 Cairo Summit, River Jordan Water & Fatah Raids (Stages 1–3)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Complete the spaced Do Now retrieving Nasser’s Pan-Arabism, the 1955 Czech Arms Deal, 26 July 1956 Suez nationalisation, and UNEF’s buffer role in Sinai from KT 1.3.
phases.instruction: Complete the spaced Do Now retrieving Nasser’s Pan-Arabism, the 1955 Czech Arms Deal, 26 July 1956 Suez nationalisation, and UNEF’s buffer role in Sinai from KT 1.3.

phases.label: Teacher Exposition
phases.activity: Explain why relative calm on the Egyptian border shifted tension northward between 1964 and 1966: the January 1964 Cairo Summit founding the PLO, clashes over Israel’s National Water Carrier and Syrian headwater diversions, and Ba’athist Syria’s sponsorship of Yasser Arafat’s Fatah raids.
phases.instruction: Explain why relative calm on the Egyptian border shifted tension northward between 1964 and 1966: the January 1964 Cairo Summit founding the PLO, clashes over Israel’s National Water Carrier and Syrian headwater diversions, and Ba’athist Syria’s sponsorship of Yasser Arafat’s Fatah raids.

phases.phase: Phase 3: Shared Reading & Verso Spine Stages 1–3 (17 mins)
phases.label: Shared Reading & Spine
phases.activity: Shared reading of Stages 1–3 and completion of Workbook Verso Spine boxes 1–3, distinguishing the Arab League’s umbrella PLO from Fatah’s independent guerrilla strategy.
phases.instruction: Shared reading of Stages 1–3 and completion of Workbook Verso Spine boxes 1–3, distinguishing the Arab League’s umbrella PLO from Fatah’s independent guerrilla strategy.

phases.phase: Phase 4: Hinge Diagnostic & Source Scrutiny (10 mins)
phases.label: Hinge Check
phases.activity: Compare Source A (the 1964 PLO Charter vs Prime Minister Levi Eshkol) with Source B (the Banias Spring headwater in Syrian-held territory) to test why water security sparked cross-border artillery strikes.
phases.instruction: Compare Source A (the 1964 PLO Charter vs Prime Minister Levi Eshkol) with Source B (the Banias Spring headwater in Syrian-held territory) to test why water security sparked cross-border artillery strikes.

lesson_2.title: Lesson 2: The Samu Raid & 7 April 1967 Dogfight (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Importance Writing) (50 mins)
lesson_2.focus: The Samu Raid & 7 April 1967 Dogfight (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Importance Writing)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Recall check on the January 1964 Cairo Summit, the National Water Carrier dispute, and Syrian backing for Fatah raids from Lesson 1.
phases.instruction: Recall check on the January 1964 Cairo Summit, the National Water Carrier dispute, and Syrian backing for Fatah raids from Lesson 1.

phases.label: Narrative & Sources
phases.activity: Read Stages 4–5 on Israel’s 13 November 1966 reprisal raid on Samu in the Jordanian West Bank and the 7 April 1967 Golan tractor clash and air battle (six Syrian MiGs shot down), analysing Sources C (Golan relief map), D (UNSC Resolution 228 on Samu), and E (rival air-battle accounts).
phases.instruction: Read Stages 4–5 on Israel’s 13 November 1966 reprisal raid on Samu in the Jordanian West Bank and the 7 April 1967 Golan tractor clash and air battle (six Syrian MiGs shot down), analysing Sources C (Golan relief map), D (UNSC Resolution 228 on Samu), and E (rival air-battle accounts).

phases.label: Exam Writing
phases.activity: Timed Edexcel Paper 2 practice: complete the 4-mark consequence question on the November 1966 Samu Raid and the 8-mark Importance question (Q3: importance of the 1964 Cairo Conference and growth of Fatah for escalating tension, 1964–67).
phases.instruction: Timed Edexcel Paper 2 practice: complete the 4-mark consequence question on the November 1966 Samu Raid and the 8-mark Importance question (Q3: importance of the 1964 Cairo Conference and growth of Fatah for escalating tension, 1964–67).

phases.label: Consolidate & DIRT
phases.activity: Review Q3 answers using DIRT to ensure pupils explain how Cairo/Fatah triggered reprisals like Samu that undermined moderate Jordan and dragged Damascus and Cairo toward crisis.
phases.instruction: Review Q3 answers using DIRT to ensure pupils explain how Cairo/Fatah triggered reprisals like Samu that undermined moderate Jordan and dragged Damascus and Cairo toward crisis.

lesson_1.title: Lesson 1: May 1967 Brinkmanship & Operation Focus (Stages 1–3) (50 mins)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Complete the spaced Do Now retrieving the 1964 Cairo Summit, National Water Carrier, Yasser Arafat’s Fatah raids, the November 1966 Samu Raid, and the 7 April 1967 air clash from KT 2.1.
phases.instruction: Complete the spaced Do Now retrieving the 1964 Cairo Summit, National Water Carrier, Yasser Arafat’s Fatah raids, the November 1966 Samu Raid, and the 7 April 1967 air clash from KT 2.1.

phases.label: Teacher Exposition
phases.activity: Walk through the three-week escalation of May 1967: the false 13 May Soviet warning of Israeli brigades on Syria’s border, Nasser expelling UNEF (16 May) and closing the Straits of Tiran (22 May), King Hussein’s 30 May Joint Defence Pact, and Israel’s pre-emptive air strike (Operation Focus) at 07:45 on 5 June.
phases.instruction: Walk through the three-week escalation of May 1967: the false 13 May Soviet warning of Israeli brigades on Syria’s border, Nasser expelling UNEF (16 May) and closing the Straits of Tiran (22 May), King Hussein’s 30 May Joint Defence Pact, and Israel’s pre-emptive air strike (Operation Focus) at 07:45 on 5 June.

phases.phase: Phase 3: Shared Reading & Verso Spine Stages 1–3 (17 mins)
phases.label: Shared Reading & Spine
phases.activity: Read Stages 1–3 and complete Workbook Verso Spine boxes 1–3, tracing why encirclement and failed Western naval diplomacy convinced Eshkol and Defence Minister Moshe Dayan to strike first.
phases.instruction: Read Stages 1–3 and complete Workbook Verso Spine boxes 1–3, tracing why encirclement and failed Western naval diplomacy convinced Eshkol and Defence Minister Moshe Dayan to strike first.

phases.phase: Phase 4: Hinge Diagnostic & Source Scrutiny (10 mins)
phases.label: Hinge Check
phases.activity: Scrutinise Source A (Nasser and Eshkol on closing the Straits of Tiran) alongside Source B (the 30 May Egyptian-Jordanian Defence Pact) to test why diplomatic off-ramps closed before 5 June.
phases.instruction: Scrutinise Source A (Nasser and Eshkol on closing the Straits of Tiran) alongside Source B (the 30 May Egyptian-Jordanian Defence Pact) to test why diplomatic off-ramps closed before 5 June.

lesson_2.title: Lesson 2: Sinai, East Jerusalem & Golan Victory (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Narrative Writing) (50 mins)
lesson_2.focus: Sinai, East Jerusalem & Golan Victory (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Narrative Writing)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Spaced recall check on the 13 May Soviet intelligence report, UNEF expulsion, 22 May Tiran closure, 30 May Jordan Pact, and Operation Focus.
phases.instruction: Spaced recall check on the 13 May Soviet intelligence report, UNEF expulsion, 22 May Tiran closure, 30 May Jordan Pact, and Operation Focus.

phases.label: Narrative & Sources
phases.activity: Read Stages 4–5 on how total air supremacy enabled Israeli armoured divisions to sweep Sinai and Gaza, capture East Jerusalem and the West Bank after Jordanian shelling (5–8 June), and storm the Syrian Golan Heights (9–10 June), interrogating Sources C, D, and E.
phases.instruction: Read Stages 4–5 on how total air supremacy enabled Israeli armoured divisions to sweep Sinai and Gaza, capture East Jerusalem and the West Bank after Jordanian shelling (5–8 June), and storm the Syrian Golan Heights (9–10 June), interrogating Sources C, D, and E.

phases.label: Exam Writing
phases.activity: Timed Edexcel Paper 2 practice: answer the two 4-mark consequence prompts (events of 7 April 1967; outbreak of the Six-Day War) and the 8-mark Analytical Narrative (Q2: key events leading up to and during the Six-Day War, May–June 1967).
phases.instruction: Timed Edexcel Paper 2 practice: answer the two 4-mark consequence prompts (events of 7 April 1967; outbreak of the Six-Day War) and the 8-mark Analytical Narrative (Q2: key events leading up to and during the Six-Day War, May–June 1967).

phases.label: Consolidate & DIRT

lesson_1.title: Lesson 1: Occupied Territories, Khartoum & UN Resolution 242 (Stages 1–3) (50 mins)

phases.activity: Explain how June 1967 transformed the conflict: Israel now administered Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem, and the Golan Heights alongside over a million Palestinians and 300,000+ new refugees, prompting Khartoum’s “Three Noes” (August–September 1967) and UN Resolution 242 (22 November 1967).

phases.instruction: Read Stages 1–3 and complete Workbook Verso Spine boxes 1–3, unpacking Lord Caradon’s “Land for Peace” formula and why omitting “the” before “territories occupied” created rival interpretations.

phases.instruction: Compare Source A (CIA post-June 1967 territorial map) with Source B (the Khartoum Resolution’s “no peace, no recognition, no negotiations” vs Israeli reactions) to diagnose diplomatic deadlock.

lesson_2.title: Lesson 2: Bar-Lev Line & Early Settlements (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Importance Writing) (50 mins)
lesson_2.focus: Bar-Lev Line & Early Settlements (Stages 4–5 & Paper 2 Importance Writing)

phases.label: Spaced Retrieval Starter
phases.activity: Quick recall check on the five territories occupied in June 1967, the Khartoum “Three Noes”, and the wording dispute inside UN Resolution 242.
phases.instruction: Quick recall check on the five territories occupied in June 1967, the Khartoum “Three Noes”, and the wording dispute inside UN Resolution 242.
